newsitem.title: UK: Carlton gains after Westcountry TV purchase.
newsitem.headline: Carlton gains after Westcountry TV purchase.

text.p: Shares in Carlton Communications Plc rose in early trading on Monday after the company pipped rival United News & Media Plc at the post to take control of privately-owned Westcountry Television.
Carlton was up 10p at 518-1/2 by 0820 GMT while United News was up 1p at 683-1/2.

Carlton said it made an agreed offer to acquire Westcountry Television Ltd for 85 million pounds in cash. It said it had received irrevocable acceptances accounting for 77 percent of Westcountry's issued share capital.
The deal makes Carlton Britain's biggest independent TV company, broadcasting to 38 percent of the population.
Analysts welcomed the deal but said it was unlikely to lead to upgrades ahead of Carlton's full-year figures next week.
"It looks a nice deal in that it's earnings positive in an industry where doing that is quite difficult," said one analyst who asked not to be named.
"It strengthens Carlton's position in the ITV network and opens up opportunities for cost savings on transmission, programming and so forth without too much risk," he said.

Analysts added that Carlton's shares were likely to benefit from what one called a "sense of relief" that Carlton, which had lagged others in the industry in mergers and acquisitions, had snatched the deal away from United.
But the upside potential for Carlton -- and the downside for United shares -- was likely to be limited because the deal was relatively small, one warned.
